accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA GCSE Physics 8463 spec 4.5.7.1 (momentum = mass × velocity, p = m v, kg m/s; higher tier) and the topic's NGSS HS-PS2-2 link. Hand-checked every number: 2 × 6 = 4 × 3 = 12; 2000 × 0.35 = 700 = 70 × 10; 2000 × 5 = 10 000; 2 × 2 + 2 × (−2) = 0; 0.5 × 4 = 2 (and ½ × 0.5 × 4² = 4 J); 1200 × 15 = 18 000; 0.16 × 40 = 6.4 vs 70 × 1.5 = 105; ½ × 2000 × 25 = 25 000 J.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented momentum errors: faster always means more momentum, adding m and v, unconverted grams, dropping the sign for motion in the negative direction, confusing p with kinetic energy (doubling v quadruples p; answers in J), and dividing m by v.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmom is a drag-the-velocity-arrow sandbox with signed momentum bars and a running vector total; the energy labs flagkeq and flagkemv show ½mv² stores, flagcoll is about particle collisions in reactions, and the force labs draw forces not momentum. Lab gate shingle overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds by dragging that 2 kg at 6 m/s equals 4 kg at 3 m/s, that a 2000 kg truck needs only 0.35 m/s to match a cyclist's 700 kg m/s, that reversing a cart flips its bar and zeroes the total, and that the bar exactly doubles when the speed doubles.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'the 2 kg cart, it is faster', 'the cyclist: 10 times faster', '6 kg m/s' for opposite motion, and 'goes up 4 times' for doubled speed.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge items whose wrong answers come from named slips tagged add, ke, gram, sign, div, sq and same; each tag has its own message (for example 'That is ½mv², the kinetic energy (in J)' and 'Change grams to kilograms first').

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences with the GCSE terms mass, velocity, vector, kg m/s and sign; kid and adult FK within the learner targets (6.5 and 9.5) checked by validate_lessons; adult text names the spec point, the link to impulse and conservation, and five mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean; each kid paragraph does one job (definition, units with a worked value, mass vs speed, direction and sign) and each lab step adds one new idea with its own numbers.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px each lane is a full-width drag zone, the arrow tip has a 10 px handle, the truck lane uses a larger velocity scale so 0.05 m/s steps are about 10 px, readouts are 12 px bold; checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in both themes.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has button twins (◀/▶ per cart, answer buttons for the units step); the canvas aria-label states each body's mass, velocity and momentum after every change; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes.

sources: AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification 4.5.7.1 Momentum is a property of moving objects: p = m v, momentum in kilogram metre per second (kg m/s)
